findings.summary: The root cause the plan will record is contradicted by the code and the history: design producers already get the `Existing code:` inventory in their brief.
findings.evidence: briefs.rs:315-323: reading_sections writes `Assumptions:` (every assumption, including `Existing code: ...`) and all acceptance criteria into the producer brief at :685. check_design_existing_code (surveys.rs:1409-1451) forces every design reading to have such an assumption and a criterion requiring an existing code section that reuses or extends it. HISTORY.txt:1340 dates that check to 2026-11-01 (671bbb9). Nine of the 13 listed jobs (20261104-* through 20261111-*) are later, so the failure recurred while the producer had both the list and the criterion. The plan concedes this itself (criterion 3: 'the path appears only in the Assumptions list'). Fix: Name the cause the evidence supports. The producer gets the reader's list, which is written from the request, as an ordinary assumption. Nothing tells it to search the repository for each component, behaviour or dependency the design proposes, so anything outside that list goes unchecked until the final verdict. Write that in the doc comment, CHANGELOG and D183. Make the section's wording match it: 'the listed paths are the reader's starting point; search for each further component yourself'.
findings.location: Approach / step 2 doc comment, CHANGELOG entry, D183 (criterion 1)

findings.summary: The section does not cover the failure modes recorded by the post-check recurrences, so the class is not prevented where it now originates.
findings.evidence: The introspections after 11-01 ask for: tracing each claim about code behaviour (a refusal, a conflict, a race outcome, a landing-gate rule) to the code path that produces it (20261109-203545-vn3k, 20261111-061031-x8mv); naming the source of each headline number (20261105-172007-jsan, 20261109-020700-1s96, 20261109-061451-zg6h); and listing, for each proposed change, the function that does it today (20261110-193951-hbcg). The planned section only asks for component existence and a cache/config/limit check. Some of those jobs are measurement or regression jobs, and the plan never checks that their readings were class `design`. Fix: Add one instruction: every claim in the design about what the code or host does, and every number it relies on, names the file and function or the record source behind it. Add one assertion for it in the criterion-2/3 test. In Risks, state which recorded jobs the design gate leaves out, or say why it covers them.
findings.location: Step 2 section content and its class_of_work == "design" gate

findings.summary: The criterion's literal assertions (path, 'Existing code', 'reuse or extend') would already pass on the base brief, so the test is only failing-first if it is scoped to the new section.
findings.evidence: On the base brief the Assumptions list holds 'Existing code: crates/athena-core/src/jev.rs ...', and a realistic design reading's criterion holds 'existing code section that reuses or extends', because the reader check demands it. Fix: Take the text after `## Existing code to read before you design` and before the next `## ` heading, then assert the path and the instructions inside that slice. Alternatively assert the full heading line, which is absent on base.

findings.summary: Copying the filter creates two definitions that can drift. A shared helper in athena-data is a small change and does not alter check_design_existing_code's behaviour.
findings.evidence: surveys.rs:1329-1336 is a 6-line pure function over `Reading`, a type in athena-data, which both core and context depend on. Making existing_code_assumptions call a `Reading::existing_code_assumptions` method keeps the check's behaviour identical. The out-of-scope item forbids changing the check's behaviour, not moving a helper. Fix: Put the filter in athena-data, as a method on Reading or a free function, and call it from both crates. Otherwise keep the copy and add a test that runs both filters over the same inputs, as Decision 3 promises.

summary: The plan is mostly accurate about the code. AcceptedReading (briefs.rs:74), AcceptedReading::new (:93), reading_sections (:309), producer_brief_with_evidence (:681), existing_tests_section (:783), planner_brief (planner.rs:85), the PLANNER_REPORT_BASE_BYTES test (:3648) and existing_code_assumptions / check_design_existing_code (surveys.rs:1328/1409) all exist where the plan says. I grepped for literals that build AcceptedReading directly: the only ones are at run_pin_tests.rs:1048, send_back.rs:497 and reading.rs:3584, so the field addition is complete. D183 is the next decision number. My main objection is the root cause the plan will write down. reading_sections already prints every assumption, including the `Existing code:` lines, and every criterion, including the "existing code section that reuses or extends" criterion the reader check forces, into the producer brief. HISTORY.txt dates that check to 2026-11-01 (671bbb9), and 9 of the 13 recorded jobs come after that date. So the producer in those jobs did see the inventory. The stated cause, "never given the inventory", is false for most of the class. The later introspections point to something else: the producer never checks the design's own components, behaviour claims and cited numbers against the code. The planned section only partly covers that. Two smaller points: the criterion-3 test has to pin assertions to the new section, because the base brief already holds the path and the words "Existing code", and the copied filter is avoidable. Verdict: revise.
